channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Taliban Official Urges Takhar University Students to Practice Religion
item.description: A Taliban official responsible for Invitation and Guidance at Takhar University has reportedly urged students to practice their religion. Some students alleged the official described them as "irreligious." The meeting also reportedly discussed clothing and beard styles, reflecting the Taliban's efforts to impose their interpretation of religious practice on society.

item.title: Uzbekistan May Introduce Mandatory Deposit System for Plastic and Glass Bottles
item.description: Uzbekistan is considering a mandatory deposit system for empty plastic and glass bottles, and aluminum cans. The proposal aims to incentivize separate waste collection and increase recycling rates, which currently stand at only 6.2%. The system would involve a refundable deposit added to the product price.

item.title: Kazakhstan Restores Republic Day as National Holiday
item.description: Kazakhstan has reinstated Republic Day, celebrated on October 25, as a national holiday. The day commemorates the adoption of the Declaration of State Sovereignty in 1990, a pivotal step towards independence. President Tokayev proposed restoring the holiday's status in July 2022.

item.title: Kazakhstan Celebrates Republic Day, President Awards State Honors
item.description: Kazakhstan celebrated Republic Day with a ceremony at Akorda, where President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev addressed the nation, highlighting achievements during the years of independence. He also presented state awards to a group of citizens for their contributions.

item.title: Two New Cotton Processing Plants Open in Turkistan Region
item.description: Two additional cotton processing plants have been launched in the Syrdariya settlement of the Otyrar district, Turkistan region, as part of efforts to develop cotton farming and deepen agricultural product processing. This brings the total operational plants for the "Turkistan Tekstil" company to four. The opening ceremony was attended by the regional governor, who highlighted the importance of such projects for boosting industrial potential.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan to Increase Social Benefits and Pensions from 2027
item.description: Kyrgyzstan will increase social benefits, certain pensions, and monetary compensations starting January 1, 2027. The most significant increase is planned for people with disabilities. Other categories, including children who lost parents, Hero Mothers, WWII veterans, donors, and Chernobyl liquidators, will also see an increase. President Sadyr Japarov also ordered a three-month rent exemption for traders relocating from the 'Madina' market.

item.title: Pakistan Media Covers Uzbekistan's International Summit on Child Wellbeing
item.description: Pakistan's Associated Press of Pakistan (APP) reported on the International Summit 'Investing in Child Wellbeing: Towards Sustainable and Equitable Development for Future Generations' held in Samarkand. The summit, organized by Uzbekistan with UN and World Bank collaboration, focused on child protection, education, healthcare, and investment. The Samarkand Declaration outlined strategic goals for child welfare.

item.title: Conference Explores Central Asia-Asia-Pacific Connectivity and Cooperation
item.description: A conference in Vladivostok discussed new levels of connectivity between Central Asia and the Asia-Pacific region. Scholars and experts from various countries, including Central Asia, China, Japan, and Korea, participated. Uzbekistan's representative highlighted the region's shift towards strategic alignment and economic cooperation, driven by political trust among leaders.

item.title: US Intelligence Warns of Increased Iranian Threats in Middle East
item.description: US intelligence reports an increase in Iranian agents' activities abroad, including potential threats against American officials and diplomats even within the United States. The head of US intelligence highlighted the heightened risk, emphasizing the growing Iranian focus on targeting Americans in the Middle East.

item.title: Afghanistan Reports Rising Polio Cases, Including Young Child's Paralysis
item.description: Afghanistan faces a surge in polio cases, with 42 recorded in the first 10 months of 2026, double last year's figures. Five-year-old Zahra from Baghlan province is among those paralyzed by the disease due to lack of vaccine availability. Afghanistan and Pakistan remain the only countries where wild poliovirus has not been eradicated.

item.title: Uzbekistan Energy Minister Reviews Progress on Solar Power and Energy Storage Project
item.description: Uzbekistan's Energy Minister Sherzod Khodjaev inspected the construction of a solar power plant and energy storage system in Nurabad district, Samarkand region. The project, a collaboration with Saudi company ACWA, aims for a 1000 MW solar capacity and a 1336 MW·h storage system. The first 100 MW phase is operational, with full completion expected by the end of 2027.

item.title: Afghan Citizens and Activists Protest Forced Deportations in Germany
item.description: Afghan citizens and civil society activists in Germany have protested against the forced deportation of asylum seekers, particularly to Afghanistan. Demonstrations occurred in several German cities and airports, with protesters calling for an end to deportations, opposing expanded detention facilities, and urging Germany to uphold the right to asylum.

item.title: US Administrations Urged SpaceX to Modify Starlink Use in Conflicts
item.description: Both the Biden and Trump administrations repeatedly asked Elon Musk to alter Starlink's operations in Ukraine and the Middle East. US presidents relied heavily on the private company for foreign policy implementation during various conflicts.

item.title: France Sees Large Protests with Approximately 800,000 Participants
item.description: An estimated 800,000 people took to the streets in France today as part of a new wave of protests. The demonstrations indicate a significant level of public mobilization and discontent.

item.title: Switzerland Spent Over $16,000 Hosting Taliban Delegation for Deportation Talks
item.description: Switzerland spent more than $16,000 to host a Taliban delegation in Geneva in August 2025. The purpose was to identify Afghan citizens convicted of crimes in Switzerland for deportation. Documents show Swiss officials shared personal information, raising safety concerns for deportees.

item.title: Charlie Chaplin's Legacy Unites Filmmakers in Tashkent Event
item.description: Tashkent hosted a special international event celebrating the cinematic achievements of Central Asian and Caucasian countries, centered around the legacy of Charlie Chaplin. The program included a press conference, the Chaplin Awards ceremony, and a film screening, supported by the Ministry of Culture of Uzbekistan. The event fostered discussions on international cooperation in cinema.

item.title: Two More Cotton Processing Plants Launched in Turkestan Region
item.description: Two additional cotton processing plants, operated by "Turkistan Tokyma" LLP, have been launched in the Syrdaria settlement of the Otyrar district, Turkestan Region. This brings the company's total number of plants to four. The launch ceremony was attended by the regional governor, who highlighted the importance of agricultural product processing and value-added production.

item.title: Afghan Envoy to Switzerland Highlights UN Missions' Role in Defending Rights
item.description: Afghanistan's ambassador to Switzerland, Nasir Ahmad Andisha, stated that diplomatic missions at the UN are actively defending people's rights, especially for women and girls, and upholding international commitments. He emphasized the UN as a bastion for defending charter values against the erosion of rights under Taliban rule.

item.title: Yemen War: Houthi Claim 16 Killed in Saudi Airstrikes
item.description: The Houthi group claims that 16 people were killed in Saudi airstrikes in Yemen. This statement comes amidst the ongoing conflict and highlights the continued violence in the region.

item.title: Reed Fire Extinguished on Shore of Kapchagay Reservoir in Almaty Region
item.description: A fire in the reeds on the shore of the Kapchagay Reservoir, near Alatau city in Kazakhstan's Almaty Region, was being fought on October 24. Firefighters faced difficulties due to difficult terrain, limited access for special vehicles, wind, and approaching darkness.

item.title: UAE Closes Beaches and Coastal Areas Due to Oil Spill
item.description: All beaches and coastal areas in the Umm Al Quwain emirate of the UAE have been temporarily closed due to an oil spill from a tanker. The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment reported the incident, stating cleanup operations have begun. Residents in Sharjah and Ajman reported a foul odor.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Military Reform to Create Modern, Mobile Army
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Defense has announced the launch of a military reform aimed at building a modern, mobile, and technologically advanced army. Key changes include restructuring the armed forces, improving command systems, enhancing troop training, and strengthening the rights of military personnel.

item.title: China Successfully Launches Earth Observation Satellites
item.description: China has successfully launched two groups of satellites for remote sensing of the Earth. The satellites are designed for natural resource exploration, agricultural yield assessment, and disaster prevention. This launch marked the 673rd mission for the Long March-4B rocket carrier.

item.title: Kazakhstan and UN Discuss Strengthening Cooperation Between Nuclear-Weapon-Free Zones
item.description: Kazakhstan proposed enhancing interaction between five regional nuclear-weapon-free zones and Mongolia to advance common priorities in dialogue with nuclear states. The initiative was presented at a forum in Astana, timed to the 20th anniversary of the Semipalatinsk Treaty. Participants discussed implementing UN research recommendations and continuing dialogue with nuclear-armed states.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Military Reform, Modifying Conscription and Modernizing Army
item.description: Kazakhstan has initiated a military reform plan aimed at changing conscript training, technologically re-equipping the army, and enhancing soldiers' rights. The reform includes a two-stage conscription model: six months of basic training and six months of service in military units. The goal is to create a modern, mobile, and technologically advanced army.

item.title: Kazakhstan Launches Military Reform with New Conscription Model and Tech Focus
item.description: Kazakhstan has initiated a military reform plan approved by the Security Council, chaired by President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. The reform introduces a new model for conscript service, changes the Armed Forces structure, develops drone technology, and enhances soldier rights protection, according to the Ministry of Defense.

item.title: Kazakhstan Initiates Military Reform, Introducing New Model for Conscript Service
item.description: Kazakhstan has begun implementing a military reform plan approved by the Security Council, focusing on modernizing the army's structure, readiness, and service regulations. The Ministry of Defense reported that the reform aims to create a mobile, technologically advanced military, prioritizing service safety and efficient resource use. It includes updating the armed forces' structure and improving defense planning.

item.title: Iran's Ambassador Summoned to Uzbek Foreign Ministry Over Statements on Samarkand's Heritage
item.description: Iran's Ambassador to Uzbekistan, Muhammad Ali Iskandariy, was summoned to the Foreign Ministry and handed a note of protest regarding statements made by Iranian diplomatic missions abroad. These missions linked Samarkand's historical and cultural heritage to Persian civilization, which Uzbekistan views as a politicized interpretation.

item.title: Uzbekistan Summons Iranian Ambassador Over Remarks on Samarkand's Heritage
item.description: Uzbekistan summoned Iran's ambassador to protest statements made by Iranian diplomatic missions regarding Samarkand's historical sites. The Foreign Ministry stated that remarks claiming Registan's arches are characteristic of "Iranian-Islamic civilization" were a one-sided and politicized interpretation of Uzbekistan's cultural heritage. The ambassador was handed a note of protest.

item.title: Central Asia-China Forum Discusses High-Quality Development and Modernization
item.description: The VI Central Asia-China Analytical Centers Forum, held in Bishkek on October 22-23, 2026, focused on "High-Quality Development and Joint Modernization." Organized by Chinese and Kyrgyz institutions, the forum brought together experts from China and five Central Asian nations. Discussions covered joint modernization, transport and digital connectivity, industrial cooperation, AI implementation, human capital, and humanitarian cooperation. Bakhtiyor Mustafayev highlighted opportunities in waste processing and resource reuse.

item.title: Iran Develops Plan to Strike Underwater Cables if War Resumes
item.description: Iran has developed a detailed plan to strike underwater cables in the Persian Gulf if a war restarts, aiming to disrupt communications and prevent repairs. The Islamic Republic has warned Washington against 'playing with fire.' This comes amid heightened regional tensions.

item.title: UN Warns Global Warming Threshold of 1.5°C Will Inevitably Be Exceeded
item.description: The UN Environment Programme (UNEP) reports that the world will inevitably exceed the 1.5°C global warming threshold under current climate policies, potentially reaching 2.8°C this century. While exceeding the limit is unavoidable, UNEP suggests measures to limit the duration and magnitude of the overshoot.

item.title: First 24-Hour Youth Community Center Opens in Almaty
item.description: Almaty has launched its first round-the-clock community center for youth. The center aims to provide a space for young people to learn, work on projects, create content, and connect with peers at any hour. This initiative supports the city's 'Sleepless City' concept, focusing on developing 24-hour urban infrastructure.

item.title: Amir Temur's Legacy Discussed at Beijing University
item.description: The Director of the Institute of History of the Academy of Sciences of Uzbekistan, Azamat Ziyo, delivered a lecture at Beijing Minzu University on the history of the Timurid dynasty in Central Asia. The event focused on the role of Amir Temur in Uzbek history, the formation of national statehood, and his historical legacy. Participants also discussed historical sources and current research.

item.title: Pakistani Forces Kill Two Drivers on Chaman-Spin Boldak Route
item.description: Sources in Afghanistan's Spin Boldak district report that Pakistani military personnel shot and killed two Afghan drivers. The drivers were attempting to enter Afghanistan illegally with the consent of Pakistani forces and the Taliban. Smuggling routes are reportedly being used for travel between the two countries following the Taliban's closure of official crossing points.

item.title: Kazakhstan Reviews Seven Years of Reforms Under President Tokayev
item.description: Since Kassym-Jomart Tokayev assumed the presidency in 2019, Kazakhstan has undergone significant changes in its political structure, economy, and social sectors. Reforms have updated the constitution, revised the governance system, and introduced new mechanisms for protecting citizens' and entrepreneurs' rights. Social support, education, healthcare, and tax systems have also been modernized.

item.title: Kazakhstan to Halve Maximum Duration of Unemployment Benefit Payments
item.description: Starting January 1, 2027, Kazakhstan will reduce the maximum duration for receiving unemployment benefits from six to three months. The Ministry of Labor and Social Protection announced that payments will depend on the duration of participation in the social insurance system, with a cap of 45% of seven times the minimum wage.

item.title: Kazakhstan May Revoke Foreign Journalists' Accreditation Over National Security Concerns
item.description: Kazakhstan is tightening accreditation rules for foreign media and journalists, with the Ministry of Foreign Affairs to have increased oversight. Foreign media offices must now submit annual reports. The ministry can deny or revoke accreditation based on "national security interests," though specific criteria are not detailed.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Explains 12-Year Education Reform Using Son's University Admission
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's President Sadyr Japarov explained the necessity of transitioning to a 12-year school education system using a personal example. He recounted that his son had to attend a preparatory year after 11th grade before entering a European university. The reform, initiated in 2023, aims to improve educational quality and school management, with the first diplomas expected in June 2028.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Publicly Criticizes Education Minister Dogdourkul Kendirbaeva
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov publicly criticized the management of Kyrgyzstan's education system during a meeting with residents. He stated that problems stem from poor management and lack of digitalization, not strategy. Japarov specifically criticized Education Minister Dogdourkul Kendirbaeva, citing issues with textbook distribution in Naryn as an example and demanding digitalization of school data.
